key_insight: ST2M guides crystal generation with crystallographic symmetry, improving the joint yield of stable, unique, and novel structures.
engineering_relevance: The model could accelerate materials discovery by generating chemically viable crystal candidates under prescribed crystallographic constraints.
method: Represent crystals as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits.
Use Wyckoff-pattern conditioning and degree-of-freedom masks to constrain generation.
Jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables with a twin-branch Transformer.
evidence_signal: ST2M reports 96.37% structural validity and a 23.86% stable–unique–novel yield for known patterns, 68.15% better than the strongest baseline; first-principles calculations identify 21 previously unreported stable structures among selected low-predicted-energy candidates.
watch_item: The reported joint yield applies to known patterns, while first-principles validation covers selected candidates; performance on unknown patterns and experimental synthesizability require further assessment.
paper_title: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
